skill_title: Investigate impact of rate changes or extra repayments
notes: Compare baseline vs modified scenarios (rate change, higher repayment, lump sum). Total cost or time-to-repay impact.

stimulus.inline: **Baseline loan: R10 000 at 1%/month, repaying R500/month — takes ~22 months to settle.**

items.question: If the interest rate rises to 1,5%/month (and repayment stays at R500), what will happen to the time taken to settle?
workingSteps: Higher interest = more added to balance each month.
Same repayment now covers less capital each month.
So loan takes longer to clear.

stimulus.inline: **Baseline R10 000 loan at 1%/month, R500/month. Now consider raising repayment to R750/month.**

items.question: How does the higher repayment affect (a) time to settle, (b) total interest paid?
workingSteps: More repayment per month = more capital paid down faster.
Smaller balance each month earns less interest.
Loan clears sooner AND less interest accumulates.

stimulus.inline: **R20 000 loan at 1%/month. Compare repayments of R500/month vs R1 000/month.**

items.question: Calculate the closing balance after 3 months under each repayment schedule.
workingSteps: Higher repayment → ~R1 500 lower balance after 3 months.

stimulus.inline: **A R900 000 home loan over 20 years at 10,5% per annum compound has a baseline monthly payment of R8 985.**

items.question: If the borrower increases the monthly payment to R10 000 (R1 015 extra/month), describe the qualitative effect on total interest paid over the life of the loan.
items.expectedAnswer: The extra R1 015/month goes directly to paying down the capital faster. Less capital outstanding each month means less interest is calculated, and the loan settles years earlier than 20. Total interest paid over the life of the loan drops substantially — typically by R200 000-R400 000 on a R900k bond, depending on exact rates. The extra payment is one of the most powerful tools for reducing home-loan cost.
workingSteps: Identify that extra payment goes 100% to capital reduction.
Faster capital reduction = less interest each subsequent month.
Total interest reduces by a much larger amount than the extra payment over time.

stimulus.inline: **A R50 000 study loan at 0,8%/month, R1 000/month repayment.**

items.question: What is the closing balance after 6 months at baseline rate?
workingSteps: Build the table month by month with 0,8% interest then R1 000 repayment.
Continuing 6 months → approximately R46 436.

stimulus.inline: **Same R50 000 study loan. After 6 months the bank raises the rate from 0,8% to 1,0% per month. Repayment stays R1 000.**

items.question: What is the closing balance after 9 months total (3 months at the new rate)?
workingSteps: Start month 7 with R46 436,96 opening.

stimulus.inline: **Loan: R30 000 at 1%/month, R1 200/month repayment.**

items.question: Compare two scenarios: (a) pay just the R1 200/month for 12 months, (b) pay R1 200/month AND make a lump-sum payment of R3 000 at the start of month 6. Which leaves a lower balance at the end of month 12?
workingSteps: Scenario (a): build 12-month table; final balance ≈ R17 950.
Scenario (b): same 5 months, then drop balance by R3 000 at start of M6 (or with M6 repayment), then continue. Final balance ≈ R14 650.
Lump sum reduces both principal AND all subsequent interest → ~R3 300 better off (R3 000 + ~R300 saved interest).

stimulus.inline: **Why is making a lump-sum payment EARLY in a loan more beneficial than LATE?**

items.question: Explain in your own words.
items.expectedAnswer: Interest is calculated on the outstanding balance every month. If you pay R5 000 off early (say in month 2), that R5 000 stops earning interest for the bank for the remaining 58+ months of the loan — saving a lot of interest. If you pay the same R5 000 only in month 50, it only saves you interest for the last 10 months. Earlier lump sums avoid more months of compounding interest, so the total saving is much larger.
workingSteps: Identify that interest accumulates month after month on outstanding balance.
Earlier capital reduction avoids more months of interest.
Late payment can only avoid the remaining few months of interest.

items.question: What is the closing balance after 4 months at baseline?

items.question: What is the closing balance after 8 months total (4 baseline + 4 higher)?
workingSteps: Start month 5 with R6 650 (approx).

stimulus.inline: **Cumulative impact on a R100 000 loan at 12%/year (1%/month) over 5 years.**

items.question: If the interest rate rises by 1 percentage point (to 13% per annum / 1,083%/month), describe the impact on the monthly repayment needed to clear the loan in the same time.
workingSteps: Higher interest means more interest added each month.
To clear the loan in the same time, more must be paid each month.

stimulus.inline:
**Three scenarios for a R200 000 car loan over 5 years (60 months):**
- Scenario 1: 10% per annum, R4 248/month.
- Scenario 2: 12% per annum, R4 449/month.
- Scenario 3: 14% per annum, R4 656/month.

items.question: Calculate the TOTAL paid over the 60 months under each scenario and identify the cheapest.
workingSteps: Lower rate = lower total repayment. S1 cheapest.

stimulus.inline: **Same car loan scenarios above.**

items.question: How much MORE does Scenario 3 (14%) cost compared to Scenario 1 (10%) in TOTAL?
workingSteps: A 4-point rate difference on a R200k loan over 5 years costs ~R24 500 extra.

stimulus.inline: **Same R200 000 car loan @ 12% per annum. Baseline: 60 months at R4 449/month → total R266 940.**

items.question: If Sandile increases his monthly payment by R500 (to R4 949), explain how this would affect the loan's total cost and term.
items.expectedAnswer: Paying R500 more per month means each repayment knocks more off the capital. The capital reduces faster, so the interest charged each subsequent month is on a smaller balance. The loan would clear in fewer months — likely around 53 months instead of 60. Total paid would still be less than R266 940 because the saved interest exceeds the small extra paid each month. Estimated total interest saving: R10 000-R15 000.
workingSteps: Identify R500 extra/month goes to capital.
Capital falls faster → less interest each month.
Loan term shortens; total interest reduces.
Estimate scale.

stimulus.inline:
**Mortgage scenarios — R1 000 000 home loan over 20 years:**
- 10% per annum: monthly payment R9 650, total R2 316 000.
- 11% per annum: monthly payment R10 322, total R2 477 280.
- 12% per annum: monthly payment R11 010, total R2 642 400.

items.question: How much extra interest does the 12% rate generate vs the 10% rate over the 20-year loan?
workingSteps: A 2-point higher rate over 20 years on R1m principal costs an extra R326 400 in total.

stimulus.inline:
**Sipho has a R600 000 home loan at 10,5% per annum over 20 years (monthly payment R5 992, total R1 438 080).**

He inherits R50 000 and wonders whether to (a) keep it in savings at 7% compound interest or (b) pay it as a lump sum off his home loan.

items.question: Which is the better financial decision, and why?
items.expectedAnswer: Pay it off the home loan. The home loan rate (10,5%) is significantly higher than the savings rate (7%). Money paid off the bond effectively 'earns' the interest rate the bond is charging — so paying R50 000 off a 10,5% loan saves him more interest than the same R50 000 would earn in a 7% savings account. The extra 3,5 percentage points compounded over the remaining loan life is substantial — many tens of thousands of Rand. The only reason to keep it in savings is if you need it as emergency liquid funds.
workingSteps: Compare loan rate vs savings rate.
Higher loan rate means paying it down saves more than the savings would earn.
Note the liquidity trade-off as caveat.

stimulus.inline: **R15 000 personal loan at 1,2%/month, R750/month baseline repayment.**

items.question: How much is the closing balance reduced if a R2 000 lump sum is added to the month 3 repayment? Compare against the baseline month 3 closing.
workingSteps: Baseline M3 closing ≈ R13 041 (from running the table 3 months).
With lump sum added in M3: closing reduces by exactly the R2 000 lump-sum amount (same opening, same interest, same standard repayment, then extra R2 000 deducted).
Reduction = R2 000 directly, plus the lump sum begins saving interest from M4 onwards.

stimulus.inline: **Investment scenario: R5 000 at 0,6%/month, R200/month contribution.**

items.question: How much MORE will the balance be after 12 months if Pretty doubles her monthly contribution to R400?
workingSteps: 12 extra months × R200 extra contribution = R2 400 extra contributed.
Plus small extra interest on the higher balance over the year.
Total extra ≈ R2 400 + small interest gain.

stimulus.inline: **R12 000 hire purchase at 1,8%/month, R600/month repayment.**

items.question: If the rate drops from 1,8% to 1,4%/month after 4 months, what is the closing balance after a total of 6 months?

stimulus.inline: **Why is increasing your monthly repayment generally the most powerful tool for reducing total cost of a loan?**

items.question: Explain.
items.expectedAnswer: Every extra rand of monthly repayment goes 100% to capital reduction. Lower capital means less interest charged in every subsequent month. The saved interest compounds — interest you didn't pay in month 4 also wasn't there to grow in month 5, 6, 7, etc. So a small ongoing increase in repayment leads to a much larger total saving over the life of the loan than the extra amount paid would suggest. It also shortens the loan term, ending the interest-charging period sooner.
workingSteps: Identify extra payments go to capital, not interest.
Lower capital → less interest each subsequent month.
Compounding saving over remaining term.
Loan term shortens.

stimulus.inline: **R3 000 retail credit at 2%/month, R300/month repayment.**

items.question: How many months will it take to fully repay?
workingSteps: Build the table; balance reduces each month.
Continuing 12 months → balance drops to ~R0. Final months may have small remaining repayment.
Roughly 12 months to settle.

stimulus.inline: **Same retail account, R3 000 at 2%/month. Compare paying R300/month vs paying R500/month.**

items.question: How many months less does the higher repayment take? Roughly how much total interest does it save?
workingSteps: R300/month: ~12 months to settle, total paid ≈ R3 600 (~R600 interest).
R500/month: ~7 months to settle, total paid ≈ R3 350 (~R350 interest).
Saves ~5 months and ~R250 in interest.

stimulus.inline:
**Two savings strategies, both at 0,5%/month, both for 12 months:**
- Strategy A: R5 000 lump sum at start, no further deposits.
- Strategy B: R0 start, R450/month contribution.

items.question: Calculate the closing balance under each.
workingSteps: Strategy B: contributions total 12 × R450 = R5 400 plus compound interest on growing balance ≈ R5 563. (Builds via the same model approach as L4.T4.A3 items.)

stimulus.inline: **Long-term retirement comparison: Starting at age 25 vs starting at age 35, both saving R500/month at 8% per annum compound until retirement at age 65.**

items.question: Roughly, how much MORE will the early starter have at age 65?
items.expectedAnswer: Starting at 25 gives 40 years of compounding; starting at 35 gives 30 years. With R500/month at 8% p.a. compound, starting at 25 results in roughly R1,75 million; starting at 35 results in roughly R750 000. The early starter has approximately R1 million more, despite only contributing 10 × 12 × R500 = R60 000 more. The extra R940 000 is purely from compounding interest over those additional 10 years.
workingSteps: Estimate future value of monthly annuity at each time horizon.
40 years compounding vs 30 years compounding.
Note that the extra contribution (R60k) is small compared to the extra wealth (~R1m).
Conclusion: starting early is the single most powerful retirement saving decision.

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_REPAYMENT_IMPACT: Misunderstands the effect of a change in repayment amount (e.g. assumes higher repayment makes total interest higher)
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_RATE_DIRECTION: Misunderstands the direction of impact when interest rate changes
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_REPAYMENT_BEFORE_INTEREST: Subtracts the repayment from the opening balance BEFORE adding the interest
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_BALANCE_GROWTH_BASE: Calculates interest on the wrong balance
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_COMPOUND_AS_SIMPLE: Models a multi-year scenario as simple interest when compound is required
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_SUBTRACTION_ORDER: Subtracts in the wrong order when computing differences
